requirement:
Pass the `next` UUID exactly as returned by the previous page. The UUID
identifies the prepared result and determines the shape of the returned object.

```text
get_next_page({uuid: UUID}) -> object
```
rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.pages.mcp` has three obligations. I found a test for each.

1. **The tool is `get_next_page({uuid: UUID}) -> object`.** `default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs` checks that the tool list contains `get_next_page`. It also asserts the exact schema, `{type: object, required: [uuid], properties: {uuid: {type: string, format: uuid}}}`. `application_tools_preserve_graph_tools_in_the_same_conversation` shows `get_next_page` is offered on every request in a conversation that also has application tools.

2. **The caller passes the `next` UUID exactly as returned.** Every paging test feeds the `next` value taken from the previous page straight back into `get_next_page`:
   - `listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing` follows `page["next"]` through 2000 files.
   - `outline_continuations_keep_the_file_and_complete_ordered_items` follows `next` for both outline pages and read_node text pages.
   - `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` follows `first["next"]` for search pages.
   - In `application_tools_preserve_graph_tools_in_the_same_conversation`, the scripted call is `{"use_next":true}`. The harness replaces it with the value returned by the previous page (`returned_node_page`). The test then asserts the delivered text and a new valid `next` UUID.

3. **The UUID identifies the prepared result and determines the shape of the returned object.** The tests assert a different shape for each kind of result, all through `get_next_page`:
   - Listings return `files` entries with `node` and `data`.
   - Outlines return `items` with `node`, `file`, `selector` and `kind`.
   - Node reads return `text`, `children` and `next`.
   - Searches return `matches`, `search_id` and `next`.
   
   Each continuation keeps the originating result's shape and snapshot. The files change on disk after the first page and the pages still come from the original result. The outline test asserts a malformed UUID and an unknown UUID are rejected. The search test asserts a UUID from another session is rejected. These errors, reuse of a UUID and the `next` field's presence are governed by the sibling requirements `pages.behavior` and `pages.mcp.description`, not by the subject.

All of these tests carry a `{test}` reference to the subject. I found no unreferenced relevant test and no acknowledgments. The remaining paging obligations belong to sibling requirements, so I did not assess them here.

Pass the `next` UUID exactly as returned by the previous page. The UUID
identifies the prepared result and determines the shape of the returned object.
```text
get_next_page({uuid: UUID}) -> object
:::{req} pages.mcp.description
> `Pass the UUID from next to read the next page in the same format. When next
> is absent, this is the last page.`
:::{req} pages.inputs
A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. Each continuation of a
node or mapped source read retains the original node identity and content
fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version. A change
to that node's fingerprint can invalidate the evidence even if it happens
between pages. Agent tools record on delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence
inputs, just like their initial result. Preparing an undelivered page records
no read.
:::{req} pages.behavior
Each page has the same result fields as the originating tool. Text reads return
successive portions of text. Listings, outlines, and searches return successive
arrays of whole entries in their original order. Only a page with a successor
includes `next`.
Reusing a UUID returns the same page from the original snapshot, including the
same successor UUID if more remains. A malformed UUID, an unknown UUID, or a UUID
from another conversation returns a tool error under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.tool_agent.isolation`.
